subject.title: [Feature]: Channel plugin threading policy for automatic subagent parameter injection

question: Should OpenClaw add a channel-declared auto-injection policy for `sessions_spawn` thread/session parameters, or should this wait for the broader persistent-session/thread-binding contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing defaults and SDK shape changes public plugin behavior and can alter routing, persistence, and message delivery for existing users.

options.title: Design unified SDK/session policy first
options.body: Settle the thread-binding and persistent-session contract across current and child-placement channels before implementing auto-injection fields or defaults.

options.title: Keep explicit tool parameters only
options.body: Leave models/operators responsible for `thread` and `mode` until a stronger product need justifies implicit routing changes.

options.title: Queue a narrow auto-injection implementation
options.body: Add a small channel metadata policy now, accepting that later session-decoupling work may revise the API.

recommendation.title: Design unified SDK/session policy first
recommendation.body: Settle the thread-binding and persistent-session contract across current and child-placement channels before implementing auto-injection fields or defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent core refactor moved this behavior into core and defines the architecture any new policy would extend.
